chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm, who said: Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them) said:

Five traditions are related to the head, and five traditions are related to the body. As for those in the head: using the siwak (toothstick), shaving the moustache, parting the hair, gargling, and inhaling water into the nose. And as for those in the body: circumcision, shaving pubic hair, plucking the armpit hair, clipping the nails, and washing up after relieving oneself.

key_terms.الاسْتِنْشَاقُ: Inhaling water into the nose during wudu
key_terms.السِّوَاكُ: Using a toothstick for oral hygiene
key_terms.الِاسْتِنْجَاءُ: Washing the private parts after relieving oneself

ai.seo_question: What are the five sunnah practices for the head and the five for the body according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this hadith from Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) systematizes ten key aspects of *fitrah* (natural disposition), linking physical cleanliness to spiritual purity. It reflects the Shia emphasis on the Prophet’s household as the source of practical jurisprudence, where grooming and hygiene are elevated to acts of worship. This categorization underscores the holistic Islamic view that bodily care is an integral component of religious observance and social etiquette.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 5-11 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Faz’zal, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn al-Jahm, on the authority of Abul Hassan Musa ibn Ja’far (MGB), “

Five traditions are related to the head, and five traditions are related to the body. The five related to the head are: brushing the teeth; shaving the moustache; parting one’s hair; gargling; and taking water into the nose. The five traditions related to the body are: circumcision; shaving pubic hair; trimming underarm hair; clipping one’s nails; and washing up after going to the toilet.”
